title: Every Developer Posts the Same Launch Video. Here Is What to Show Instead
seoTitle: Every Developer Posts the Same Video: Do This Instead
description: Drone shot, pool, champagne. Every presale launch video looks the same and buyers forget them. Learn what to film instead so buyers picture their own life.
answer: Most real estate developers post the same launch video: a drone shot, the pool and champagne on the terrace. Buyers have seen it many times and remember none of it. What they have never seen is their own life inside your building. Show the morning coffee on their terrace and the view from their bed when they wake up, not just the amenities.
body:
Scroll through the launch videos of ten new towers and you will see the same film ten times. It looks expensive. It is also forgettable, and that is a real problem when you need buyers to commit to something that is not built yet.

## The launch video everyone makes

The formula is always the same:

- A drone shot circling the tower at sunset
- A slow pan across the pool
- Champagne glasses on the rooftop terrace

None of this is bad footage. The problem is that every developer posts it, so it no longer tells a buyer anything about your building. In my experience, nobody remembers a single one of these videos a day later.

## Why luxury shots do not stand out anymore

Buyers already know what luxury looks like. They have seen thousands of pools and rooftops. Showing them one more does not create a reason to choose you. It only proves that your building has the same amenities as the one down the street.

What a buyer is really trying to decide is simple: can I see myself living here? A drone shot cannot answer that question.

## Show the life inside the unit

What buyers have never seen is their own day inside your building. That is the content that sticks. Think about the small, real moments:

1. Morning coffee on the terrace of a real unit
2. The view from the bed when you wake up
3. The light in the kitchen at breakfast
4. The walk from the front door to the living room

These moments are personal. They let a buyer stop looking at a building and start imagining a home. A pool looks the same in every tower. The view from one specific bedroom, on one specific floor, belongs only to your building, and that is what a buyer will remember when it is time to decide.

## Stop selling the building

The shift is small but important. Most launch videos sell the building. The videos that work sell the life in a specific unit. When you plan your next launch, start with one question: what will this buyer feel on a normal Tuesday morning in this apartment? Film that first. The drone shot can come later, if at all.
takeaways: Most developer launch videos use the same drone, pool and champagne shots.
Buyers have seen so many luxury amenities that these shots no longer stand out.
The real question a buyer asks is whether they can see themselves living there.
Show everyday moments inside a unit, like coffee on the terrace or the view from the bed.
Sell the life in a specific unit, not the building as a whole.
faq: What should a real estate launch video show?
It should show what daily life feels like inside a specific unit, such as the view, the light and simple morning moments, not only the amenities and drone shots.
Why do presale marketing videos fail?
Many look exactly like every other developer's video, so buyers do not remember them and they give no reason to choose one building over another.
How do you market an off-plan project on social media?
Help buyers picture their own life in the unit. Personal, everyday moments are more memorable than generic luxury footage.
